newsitem.title: USA: Bermuda Commodities Exchange to open in September.
newsitem.headline: Bermuda Commodities Exchange to open in September.

text.p: The Bermuda Commodities Exchange, billing itself as a new venue to hedge and invest in catastrophic insurance risk, is set to open in September, the exchange said in a press release Monday.
The exchange, in Hamilton, Bermuda, will offer trading of options contracts based on an index of insured homeowner losses due to natural disasters in six U.S. regions over specified periods.
Trade will be in U.S. dollars.

Initially, the exchange will offer options covering six-month periods -- January through June, and July through December -- for Florida, the Northeast, the Southeast, Gulf area, Mid/West and National.
Contracts will cover damage from a single event or aggregate damage over the covered period, the exchange said.

The option buyer will pay a premium to a seller and the latter will be liable for payment if losses in the particular region and time period from hurricanes, tornadoes, windstorms, hail and freezing temperatures exceed a specific loss-to-value ratio.

The exchange said trading will be done via an automated, electronic system that connects all members in a "virtual open outcry" arrangement. The prices and quantities of all bids and offers will be displayed without disclosing the identity of members or customers.

Initial membership of the exchange is expected to include affiliates of American International Group, Chase Manhattan Bank, and Guy Carpenter & Co. Members will elect a seven-member board of directors.
The exchange said it will have up to 100 members, consisting of insurance companies, reinsurers, and commercial and investment banks.
Options contracts will be in units of $5,000 and traders will enter orders via their computer, on-site at an exchange terminal, or via phone or fax.

Currently, the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) offers options trading on a variety of catastrophe insurance contracts. No options traded Friday, and total open interest hovers around 15,000 contracts, a CBOT source said.

All financial futures and options in the U.S. fall under the jurisdiction of the Commodity Exchange Act. The Bermuda Commodities Exchange and its products will be regulated by the Bermuda Monetary Authority.
